paper.title: SMART-LLM: Smart Multi-Agent Robot Task Planning using Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: Staged LLM decomposition, coalition formation and allocation produce executable heterogeneous multi-robot plans using skill APIs, with claimed task and simulator-to-hardware generalization.

evidence.quote: we assume that robot skills, \Delta , are either pre-implemented in the system or that there are available API calls to execute these skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Low-level capabilities supplied, not learned by SMART-LLM.

evidence.quote: These plans are executed by making API calls to the robots’ low-level skills
evidence.support_explanation: Executable intermediate code dispatches external skills.
6/8/14/8 task-category sizes; not a large independent external benchmark.

evidence.quote: the example prompts were distinct from the tasks in the dataset and were based on different AI2-THOR floorplans not included in the dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit prompt-example/test tasks and floorplan separation.

evidence.quote: Our evaluations are based on the dataset’s final ground truth states, which we compare to the achieved states post-execution to assess task success.
evidence.support_explanation: Goal attainment checked using simulator final states, plus robot utilization for SR.

evidence.quote: We presume that our robots are endowed with essential low-level skills, including GoToLocation , ClickPicture , and Patrol
we conducted 5 separate runs, each on a randomly selected task from every category within our dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Repeated study covers selected tasks, not full benchmark paired intervals.
Same-backbone prompt ablations support marginal staging effects.

evidence.quote: we aim to enhance our work by implementing dynamic task allocation among robots
evidence.support_explanation: Dynamic repair is future work, not an existing control loop.

evidence.quote: our method executed it seamlessly using real robots
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative real executions have no taskwise trial denominator.
Rule allocation matches simple SR .62; no blanket every-category gain.

signatures.information: Instruction, environment/object dictionaries, robot-capability metadata and fixed stage examples (5 decomposition, 3 coalition, 4 allocation).
signatures.operation: Generate task subtasks/precedence, infer capability coalitions, allocate robots, emit Python threading/skill calls and interpret.
signatures.output: Team plan executed through low-level skill APIs
signatures.conditions: Feasible task; correct dictionaries; reliable skills; 1–4 robots in current custom benchmark.
signatures.feedback: Artifacts pass forward through stages; no execution-triggered dynamic repair loop.
signatures.selection_rule: Few-shot inferred role/capability allocation; no candidate verifier acceptance or optimizer.
signatures.selection_data: Current episode plus designer-provided few-shot/initializer data; no automatically retained harness changes.
signatures.persistence: Current plan only; designer prompt library static, not accumulated by successful runs.
signatures.later_use: Interpreter invokes selected robots; future tasks reuse unchanged prompts.
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher task completion and robot utilization without per-task planner training.
signatures.failure_boundary: Ordering/teaming errors, infeasible tasks, untested state/communication errors; coordination latency absent.

gap.author_gap: Multi-robot planning needs natural-language decomposition, coalition formation and allocation rather than rigid per-scenario manual allocation rules.
gap.checked_gap: Heterogeneous capability composition is concrete; same-decomposition random/rule baselines test allocation. Independently fixed adjacency originals absent.

claims.text: Coalition-aware staged planning improves executed multi-robot task success.
claims.baseline/control: Same GPT-4 decomposition + random/rule allocation, plus no-coalition/comments ablations.
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt examples and test tasks/floorplans explicitly disjoint.
claims.result/denominator: Table III SR .75 vs no-coalition .60; Table I complex SR .71 vs rule .14, random .00.
claims.counterevidence: Own small benchmark; no-coalition examples shift teaming; alternatives not exhaustive, cost unmatched.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive same-backbone improvement on this task distribution, not optimal or reliable large-team scheduling.

claims.text: Simulator-derived prompts generalize to hardware teams.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same prompts, new skill APIs; no documented hardware dev split.
claims.result/denominator: Qualitative hardware executions, no trial n.
claims.counterevidence: Not quantified transfer; no failure/repeat audit.
